why_it_failed.root_cause: `config` holds the SearchConfig for the whole function, and the `for entry in retained_candidates:` loop rebinds it with `config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(str(directory))`. The summary then reads `config.run_id` off a Qwen3Config. A local-name collision.
why_it_failed.why_it_never_appeared_before: that loop body only executes when `retained_candidates` is non-empty, which is PHASE B ONLY. Phase A passes none, so `config` was never rebound and every Phase-A run and every zero-cost test passed straight over it.
why_it_failed.when_it_fired: AFTER the search, the control measurement, the imported finalist measurements and the ranking. The scientific work of Stage 1 was complete; only its report was not written.
why_it_failed.class: a $0-detectable defect on a path only Phase B reaches. The same shape as the SESSION_KIND gap and the artifact-spec path: Phase-B-only code that no Phase-A run and no test ever executed.

stage_1_evidence_recovered._correction: An earlier version of this record said the journal held '5 searched + 2 composite + 2 imported finalists = 9 complete leaves'. That was wrong. Mechanically, from the latest record per state_id: EVERY record in the journal has provenance='search', and the imported Phase-A finalists are NOT in it at all.

stage_1_evidence_recovered.why_zero: `make_retained_state` builds the imported finalists outside BeamSearch and nothing appends them to the store, so attempt 4's measurements of them are not in the journal and are lost with the pod.
stage_1_evidence_recovered.the_id_coincidence: Two of the seven decomposed leaves carry state_ids identical to the Phase-A finalists — 85bde4ded2c3 and cca699c93f34. They are NOT the imported finalists appearing in the journal. State ids are content-derived, so the Phase-B search under calib.domain_balanced@v1 rediscovering the same operator composition from the same root produces the same id. That is the reproducibility contract working, and reading it as the finalists being journalled is what produced the original error.
stage_1_evidence_recovered.top_n_status: NOT REPORTED. The run computed a ranking and died before writing it, so no Top-5 artifact exists. It is reconstructible from the journal, but the journal alone is not citable candidate evidence: the restore contract requires the checkpoint BYTES with a re-derived artifact identity, and those were deleted with the pod. Reviewer decision, 2026-08-28: do not reconstruct it, do not begin sa from journal-only state ids, and do not build a one-off replay path to avoid rerunning Stage 1. A fresh complete P=2 search after the durability repair is cleaner.

telemetry_first_measurement.finding: STATE EVALUATION is 31.2% of Stage 1 — 147.2 min over 82 expansions, about 1.8 min each. The cost model prices it as pure FLOPs at roughly 0.04-0.08 min per child, so it is underpriced by more than an order of magnitude. Meanwhile the materialization overhead component I added (save+hash+reload+validate) is OVERpriced: 4.8 min actual against roughly 1 min charged per root child. The hard bound remains conservative overall, but its composition is wrong in two directions and the next pricing pass should start here.
telemetry_first_measurement.caveat: this is one run at one beam position; 82 expansions is a sample, not a law.
